content.value_statement: Complex AI tasks often exceed one agent context and create coordination failures. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code choose agent patterns with clear safeguards.
actual_capabilities: Explains supervisor, peer-to-peer, and hierarchical agent patterns.
Shows when each architecture fits complex AI workflows.
Describes context isolation as the main design goal.
Covers coordination methods such as weighted voting and debate protocols.
Lists failure modes including bottlenecks, divergence, and error propagation.
References LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI as implementation options.
limitations: Provides architecture guidance, not a runnable multi-agent framework.
Does not include complete production code or deployment automation.
Requires users to adapt patterns to their model, tools, and latency budget.
Does not validate real agent outputs or enforce runtime safety checks.

use_cases.title: Choose Agent Architecture

prompt_templates.title: Select a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the multi-agent-patterns skill to recommend one architecture for this task: [describe task]. Explain the fit, risks, and coordination needs.

prompt_templates.title: Map Agent Roles
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for a multi-step task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the multi-agent-patterns skill to split this workflow into agents: [workflow]. Define each agent purpose, inputs, outputs, and handoff rules.

prompt_templates.title: Review Failure Modes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the multi-agent-patterns skill to audit this agent design: [design]. Identify bottlenecks, divergence risks, error propagation, and missing validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced system design with safety controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the multi-agent-patterns skill to create a production coordination plan for [system]. Include context boundaries, retry limits, consensus rules, and monitoring signals.

output_examples.input: A team needs agents for market research, data analysis, and report writing.
output: Recommended pattern: supervisor architecture with direct pass-through for final expert sections.
Agents: researcher gathers sources, analyst checks evidence, writer prepares the final report.
Controls: require source validation, keep shared state small, and set retry limits for failed tasks.

output_examples.input: A support workflow must route billing, technical, and sales questions.
output: Recommended pattern: peer-to-peer handoff when the request type is clear.
Each specialist should receive the user request, current state, and a clear return condition.
Add a fallback generalist for unclear requests and a timeout to prevent circular handoffs.

output_examples.input: An enterprise planning workflow needs strategy, planning, and execution layers.
output: Recommended pattern: hierarchical architecture with strict state summaries between layers.
The strategy layer defines goals, planners create tasks, and execution agents complete atomic work.
Validate outputs at each layer before passing them downstream.

best_practices: Choose the architecture based on coordination needs and context boundaries.
Define explicit handoff protocols before adding more agents.
Validate agent outputs before another agent depends on them.
anti_patterns: Adding agents only to mirror an organization chart.
Letting every agent receive the full conversation history by default.
Using simple majority voting when agents have unequal expertise.

faq.question: What does this skill help me design?
faq.answer: It helps design multi-agent AI workflows using supervisor, peer-to-peer, and hierarchical patterns.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples, not a runtime framework.

faq.question: When should I use a supervisor pattern?
faq.answer: Use it when a task needs central planning, clear delegation, and human oversight.

faq.question: When should I use a peer-to-peer pattern?
faq.answer: Use it when tasks need flexible handoffs and requirements may change during execution.

faq.question: How does the skill address reliability?
faq.answer: It describes handoff protocols, output validation, convergence checks, and time-to-live limits.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tool-agnostic and applies to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
